fix.point: The account has no conversation at all.
fix.evidence: All 19 posts have 0 comments, including both direct questions ('Good Morning. What are you automating today?' and 'Good Afternoon. What are you currently building?'). The ranking X open-sourced in 2023 weighted replies, and replies the author answers, far above likes. The account has none.

fix.point: The 'X should not…' workflow formula is not getting responses.
fix.evidence: 9 posts use it ('An HVAC quote should never…', 'An AI agent should not run support…', 'A sales call should not end as loose notes…', 'An invoice should not be paid…' and others) and earned 4 engagements, or 0.44 per post. Both September posts in this format got 0. They read like process specs: no number, no cost, nothing to disagree with.

fix.point: Greetings that give readers nothing to respond to, and long silent gaps.
fix.evidence: 'Good Morning Everyone. Happy Tuesday.' (Sep 15) and 'Good Afternoon. What are you currently building?' (Aug 27) both got 0. Publishing has stopped twice: 59 days from Jun 14 to Aug 12, and 11 days so far since Sep 15.

12 image posts and 7 text posts both average 0.6 engagements per post. With no impression or bookmark data, we can't see whether images add dwell time. For now they cost production time with no visible return.

actions.title: Reply by hand to larger accounts for 20–30 minutes each weekday
actions.detail: Pick 15–20 active accounts in AI, automation and operations that are bigger than @arqentia. Reply within their posts' first hour with a specific point from Arqentia's work, such as a routing rule, an approval step or a failure mode, not 'great post'. This has to be done in the X app: since February 2026 the API, and so Zernio, rejects replies to accounts that have not mentioned or quoted you. Keep a weekly count of replies sent and followers, because this brief does not measure replies you send.
actions.evidence: 0 replies on all 19 posts and 0.6 engagements per post at 321 followers suggest the account's own posts are not reaching past its current followers. The expected lift from reply-led growth comes from the practitioner model; this brief does not measure it.

actions.title: Restart posting and keep two weeks queued in Zernio
actions.detail: Queue 1–2 posts per weekday (7–10 a week) so the account doesn't go quiet again. At $0.015 per post without a link, 10 posts cost about $0.15 a week.
actions.evidence: Nothing has gone out since Sep 15. August's 12 posts brought 9 of the 11 all-time engagements; September's 3 posts brought 0. There was also a 59-day gap from Jun 14 to Aug 12.

actions.title: Replace the 'X should not…' formula and plain greetings with contrarian hooks that name a cost
actions.detail: Open with the 'Most X don't have a Y problem. They have a Z problem.' pattern. Follow with one concrete scenario and a real cost from client work (hours lost, jobs double-booked, invoices paid twice); don't make numbers up. Move the step-by-step workflow detail into a self-reply thread under the post, which still works through Zernio. Drop greetings like 'Good Morning Everyone. Happy Tuesday.'
actions.evidence: The 4 'Most…' posts earned 5 engagements (1.25 per post). The 9 'X should not…' posts earned 4 (0.44 per post). 'Good Morning Everyone. Happy Tuesday.' got 0.

actions.title: Ask narrow questions, then stay online to answer every reply
actions.detail: Replace broad prompts like 'What are you currently building?' with questions that are easy to answer, for example 'Which handoff in your business still lives in one person's inbox?' Post them when someone can watch the app for the next 60 minutes and answer every reply. If it's quiet after 10 minutes, have Rafael add the first answer by hand.
actions.evidence: 'Good Morning. What are you automating today?' earned 2 engagements (tied best) but 0 replies. 'Good Afternoon. What are you currently building?' got 0 of anything.

actions.title: Put Rafael's own account in front, with @arqentia reposting
actions.detail: Post the contrarian takes and the daily replies from Rafael's personal X account, and have @arqentia repost or quote the best ones. Connect that account to Zernio with analytics on so it shows up in this brief.
actions.evidence: The brief's audience context names Rafael's personal brand, but only @arqentia's data is here, at 0.6 engagements per post. The idea that founder accounts beat brand accounts on X is a practitioner heuristic. This data doesn't show it.

actions.title: Set the X spend cap and keep links out of the main post
actions.detail: Set a monthly X spend cap in the Zernio dashboard, sized to your planned posts plus metric reads at $0.005 each. When a post needs a link, put it in a self-reply. A post with a link costs $0.20 against $0.015 without one, and main-post links tend to cut reach.
actions.evidence: The data notes say analytics are ON and the spend cap is unset. The one post with a link marker, 'La segunda vuelta en Perú…' (Jun 10), got 0 engagements. That is one post, and it can't separate the link's effect from the Spanish language's.

recommendations.cadence: Post 1–2 times each weekday (7–10 a week) and send 15–20 hand-written replies a day to larger accounts. The best-time table can't pick slots yet: it covers 19 posts, lifts only range from 0.9 to 1.2, and each top slot rests on 1–3 posts (Wed 9am–12pm at 1.2 on 2 posts; Mon 9am–12pm and Fri 3–6pm at 1.0 on 2 each; Saturday at 1.2 on 1 post). Keep one anchor post at 9–10am ET Mon–Wed, where most of the history sits. Test a second slot at 5–7pm ET and one Saturday post. Do the reply block in the hour after each post goes live. This plan comes from engagement counts only, since X returns no impressions here.

working.point: Contrarian 'Most X don't…' openers do best.
working.evidence: Four posts open this way: 'Most business owners don't need more software…' (Aug 15, 2 likes), 'Most service businesses don't have a lead problem…' (Aug 14, 1 like), 'Most operational failures aren't people problems…' (Jun 10, 1 repost) and 'Most people are still thinking in “jobs.”' (Jun 14, 1 like). Together they have 5 engagements, or 1.25 per post, about double the account's 0.6. Four posts are too few to call this proven.

working.point: A plain, open question tied for the best post.
working.evidence: 'Good Morning. What are you automating today?' (Wed Aug 26, 10am ET) got 2 engagements (1 like, 1 repost), tied for the account's highest. It still drew 0 replies.

working.point: Steady posting is when all the real engagement came.
working.evidence: August had 12 posts and 9 engagements (0.8 per post), June had 4 posts and 2 engagements, and September has 3 posts and 0 engagements. 9 of the account's 11 all-time engagements came during the Aug 12–27 run.

recommendations.headline: @arqentia's 19 posts have drawn 0 replies and 11 engagements in total, so make a daily block of hand-written replies to larger AI and automation accounts the main growth activity, and restart posting, which stopped on Sep 15.
recommendations.diagnosis: @arqentia has 321 followers and 19 posts with 11 engagements in total (8 likes, 3 reposts, 0 replies), which is 0.6 per post, and 10 of the 19 posts got nothing. The only steady stretch was August (12 posts, 9 engagements, 0.8 per post). September has 3 posts and 0 engagements, and nothing has gone out since Sep 15. That follows an earlier 59-day gap (Jun 14 to Aug 12). X returns no impressions here, so we can't tell whether posts go unseen or are seen and skipped. Every comparison below rests on counts of 0 to 2 per post and only points in a direction.

experiments.test: For 3 weeks, alternate the two formats on the same topics in the same 9–10am ET slot, with at least 6 posts of each. Leave images off both so the format is the only difference.
experiments.metric: Engagements per post (likes + replies + reposts), since impressions are not available. Current baselines: 1.25 for 'Most…' posts and 0.44 for 'X should not…' posts.
experiments.hypothesis: Contrarian 'Most X don't have a Y problem' hooks earn more engagement than the 'X should not…' workflow format.

experiments.test: For 3 weeks, split posts between 9–10am ET and 5–7pm ET. So far 10 of the 19 posts went out at 8–9am and average 0.5 engagements per post. The two evening posts, 'Most business owners…' (Sat 6pm) and 'Most service businesses…' (Fri 5pm), got 3 between them.
experiments.metric: Engagements per post in each slot. Re-check the best-time table once each slot has at least 8 posts.
experiments.hypothesis: Early-evening posts do better than the 9am default.

experiments.test: Run 2 question posts a week for 3 weeks (6 in total). Tie each question to one workflow, have Rafael seed an answer within 10 minutes, and answer every reply within the hour.
experiments.metric: Replies per post (currently 0 on all 19 posts) and how many reply threads the account answers.
experiments.hypothesis: A narrow, easy-to-answer question with a seeded first answer will get the account's first replies.

fix.point: Reach per post on the profile keeps falling on the daily schedule.
fix.evidence: Median impressions per post fell 137 → 91 → 66 (Jul → Aug → Sep). The five posts after the Aug 31–Sep 4 gap averaged 158 impressions; the seven daily posts of Sep 19–25 averaged 56 (the newest are still collecting impressions). Median engagements per post fell from 2 in July to 1 in both August and September.

75 of 87 personal posts have 0 comments. The last 30 days produced 5 comments across 21 posts, all on 3 posts. The keyword bait 'Comment TRACE and I'll send you the checklist' (Jun 18) got 0 comments. The data does not show whether Rafael replied to the comments he did get.

fix.point: Native video is the weakest format on the profile.
fix.evidence: The last 6 videos (Aug 14–Sep 22) got 3 engagements in total and a median of 50 impressions, against 85 for images and 115 for text in the same window. All-time, video averages 1.4 engagements per post, the lowest of the four formats.

fix.point: The Arqentia page gets almost no reach, and its posting appears to have stopped.
fix.evidence: 29 of 35 page posts got 0 engagements. Impressions per post fell from 19 (Jul) to 8 (Aug) to 7 (Sep). The page is set up to post daily by automation, but the data has no page post after Sep 12. The page's follower count is not available.

actions.title: Move Rafael to 4 posts a week, built around the weekend
actions.detail: Replace the daily 11am slot with Saturday and Sunday long-form text at 10–11am ET, plus two weekday posts at 12–1pm ET (Monday, and Thursday or Friday). Skip Tuesday and Wednesday, and never post twice in one day. After 3 weeks, keep the schedule if impressions per post beat 56 (the Sep 19–25 average) and engagements per post beat 1.2 (last 30 days); otherwise go back.
actions.evidence: Weekday lift: Sat 1.3, Sun 1.1, Tue 0.8, Wed 0.9. Weekend text median is 285 impressions vs 91 on weekdays. The 5 posts after a 5-day break averaged 158 impressions; the 7 daily posts of Sep 19–25 averaged 56.

actions.title: Run a first-hour comment routine on every post
actions.detail: End each post with one specific question readers can answer from their own work (e.g. 'Which step would you never let a model approve?'), not a 'comment X' request. Rafael answers every comment within the first hour with a real reply. In the 15 minutes before publishing, he leaves substantive comments on 5–10 posts from operators and founders he wants to reach. Track comments per post.
actions.evidence: 75 of 87 posts have 0 comments, and only 5 comments came in the last 30 days. The top posts by engagement are the ones with 2 or more comments: Aug 10 (4 comments, 10 engagements), Jul 11 (2, 7), Aug 15 (2, 6), Jul 17 (2, 6). 'Comment TRACE…' (Jun 18) got 0 comments.

actions.title: Pause native video on LinkedIn for 4 weeks
actions.detail: Publish this month's video scripts as weekend text posts or image posts instead, and keep the videos for short-form platforms. Check the result at the 3-week review.
actions.evidence: The last 6 videos: 3 engagements in total, median 50 impressions. In the same Aug–Sep window, images had a median of 85 impressions and text 115, each averaging 1.6 engagements per post.

actions.title: Replace recap posts with a new first-hand lesson each week
actions.detail: Stop 'I published my X on this feed last month' posts. At least once a week, write up one specific Arqentia build or client conversation, anonymized: what the operator asked for, what broke, and the number that changed. Open with a clear position, the way the Aug 10 post did. If a framework is worth repeating, repackage it once as a document (see experiments).
actions.evidence: Three recaps on consecutive days each got 0 engagements on 76–102 impressions: 'Every readiness checklist gets run top to bottom.' (Aug 24), 'Who picked the process you are automating with AI?' (Aug 25), 'Nobody's AI automation fails in the chat window.' (Aug 26). The Jul 17 follow-up that answered readers' question got 6.

actions.title: Check the page automation, then post 3 a week drawn from Rafael's proven posts
actions.detail: First confirm whether the daily automation stopped or the stats pull is missing posts, since nothing appears after Sep 12. Then post 3 a week at 9am ET (Tue, Wed, Fri). Each post adapts a Rafael post from the week before that reached at least 2 engagements, rewritten as the company's view and ending with a question. Rafael comments on it in its first hour. Connect the page follower count so page growth can be measured.
actions.evidence: Page median is 5 impressions and 0 engagements; 29 of 35 posts got nothing. Its best post by lift, 'A transcript is not a handoff.' (Sep 12), got 3.6× the median impressions and both of the page's comments.

recommendations.cadence: Rafael: 4 posts a week, at most one per day. Saturday and Sunday at 10–11am ET for long text or document posts (Saturday lift 1.3 over 17 posts; the Sat 9am–12pm block is 1.3 over 13 posts; Sunday 1.1). Two weekday posts at 12–1pm ET, on Monday and on Thursday or Friday. The midday blocks score highest (Mon 12–3pm lift 1.5 on 2 posts, Fri 1.3 on 3, Thu 1.2 on 6), but the samples are small, so treat the move from 11am as a test. Skip Tuesday (lift 0.8) and Wednesday (0.9). Arqentia: 3 posts a week at 9am ET on Tue, Wed and Fri, filling Rafael's off days. Review after 3 weeks against 56 impressions per post (Sep 19–25) and 1.2 engagements per post (last 30 days).

working.point: Posts that take a clear position on what to automate, or who owns it, get the most engagement and comments.
working.evidence: 'The most valuable AI skill right now is not prompting…' (Mon Aug 10): 10 engagements, including 4 comments, which is 5× the account median of 2. 'Small businesses do not need an “AI employee.”' (Sat Jul 11): 7 engagements on 59 impressions (11.9% ER). 'Who runs your AI automation when you are not there?' (Sat Aug 15): 6 engagements, 2 comments.

working.point: Long text posts on weekends reach the most people.
working.evidence: 7 Sat/Sun text posts had a median of 285 impressions; 10 weekday text posts had 91. All 6 personal posts above 240 impressions since Jul 22 ran on a weekend, and 5 of them were text, e.g. 'You are pasting the summary into Claude…' (Sat Sep 5, 324) and 'You can build a working AI automation in Claude in one afternoon.' (Sun Aug 9, 318 impressions, 5 engagements). Weekday lift: Sat 1.3, Sun 1.1. In Aug–Sep, text and image both average 1.6 engagements per post, but text's median reach is 115 impressions vs 85 for image.

working.point: A follow-up that answers a question readers asked works. A recap does not (see Fix).
working.evidence: 'Anthropic is turning Claude into a career ladder.' (Jul 10) got 2,197 impressions, 18% of all personal impressions. The follow-up 'You do not need a CS degree to become an AI architect.' (Jul 17) answered the question readers kept asking and got 261 impressions, 6 engagements, 2 comments and 2 saves.

working.point: On the Arqentia page, one post started a conversation.
working.evidence: 'A transcript is not a handoff.' (Sep 12) got 18 impressions (3.6× the page median of 5) and 3 engagements, including both of the page's all-time comments.

recommendations.headline: Cut Rafael's profile from a daily 11am post to 4 posts a week built around weekend text posts, because his posts are reaching fewer people each month (median impressions per post: 137 in July, 91 in August, 66 in September) while the share of viewers who engage has stayed near 2%.
recommendations.diagnosis: Rafael's profile is losing distribution, not persuasion. Median impressions per post fell from 137 (Jul) to 91 (Aug) to 66 (Sep), and the seven daily posts of Sep 19–25 averaged 56, but engagement rate held steady (1.98% last 30 days vs 2.03% all-time). Because few people see each post, most posts get almost no response: 43 of 87 all-time and 15 of the last 21 got 0–1 engagements, and 75 of 87 got no comment. That means few posts earn the early signals that widen reach. The Arqentia page is not amplifying yet: 35 posts and 340 impressions in total, a median of 5 impressions and 0 engagements per post, and no page post in the data since Sep 12. Personal data covers only posts published through Zernio, so anything Rafael posted natively (including during the Aug 31–Sep 4 gap) is missing.

experiments.test: Turn the next 4 framework posts ('5 mistakes and the fix for each' type) into 6–8 page PDF documents: 2 on Saturday at 10–11am ET and 2 on a weekday at 12–1pm ET. Alternate them with text framework posts in the same slots.
experiments.metric: Impressions and saves per post, compared with the Aug–Sep text median of 115 impressions and the all-time 0.2 saves per post (17 saves across 87 posts). Previous carousels had a median of 173 impressions ('Cisco just cut 4,000 jobs…' 394; '95% of enterprise AI pilots failed…' 269), and none has run since Jul 8.
experiments.hypothesis: Framework posts reach more people and get more saves as document carousels than as text. This rests on only 4 carousels so far.

experiments.test: For 4 weeks, publish 1–2 Spanish posts a week on the profile (Sunday, plus one weekday at 12–1pm ET). Write them for LatAm operators rather than translating that week's English post.
experiments.metric: Impressions, engagements and comments per Spanish post vs English posts in the same weeks. So far 0 of 87 profile posts have been in Spanish. The page's only Spanish post, 'Arqentia amplía su cobertura…' (Aug 6), got 24 impressions (4.8× the page median) and the page's only share.
experiments.hypothesis: Spanish posts on Rafael's profile reach Latin American business owners that his English posts miss.

experiments.test: For 4 weeks, split the weekday posts. Half open with a reader-stakes line, like 'The most valuable AI skill right now is not prompting.' Half open with a concept line, like 'An automation does not break. It drifts.' Keep format and time slot the same across both groups.
experiments.metric: Engagements and comments per post against the account median of 2 engagements. For reference, the concept openers of Sep 19 and Sep 24 got 33 and 31 impressions and 0 engagements.
experiments.hypothesis: Opening lines that name the reader's decision or role get more engagement than openers that name a process concept.

fix.point: @arqentia.inc posted less in September and its reach fell
fix.evidence: 5 posts in September against 15–17 in each of June, July and August, and nothing since Sep 19. Median reach in the last 30 days was 73 (7 posts), down from 120 in the 30 days before (13 Arqentia posts). Engagements per post fell from 13.6 to 8.1 and comments fell to 0.

fix.point: On @arqentia.inc, single-industry content does worse, and in September it made up most of the posts
fix.evidence: By my read of the captions, 12 Reels are built around one industry (HVAC, gym, restaurant, body shop, therapy, shipping, among others). Their median is 6 engagements, against 11 for the 27 owner-level Reels, and none passed 300 reach. September's 'Una silla vacía…' (dental, reach 13) and 'Lunes, 7:45 a.m.…' (pharmacy, reach 19) are the two lowest-reach posts in the account's history.

fix.point: On @arqentia.inc, 'comment' calls to action aren't producing comments, and saves are near zero
fix.evidence: 16 comments across 55 posts, 9 of them on 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' (Jul 25). 'La meta no es trabajar más horas… Coméntalo' got 0 comments on 548 reach. The guide offer in 'Es lunes a las 9…' got 3 comments on 537 reach. Saves total 8, or 0.10% of reach.

fix.point: @rgschwart, the account with the reach, is idle and has never posted a Reel
fix.evidence: 0 posts in the last 30 days and 5 posts since Nov 2025: 4 carousels and 1 image. Its one work-focused post, 'Quick Business Trip to the Windy City…' (Nov 14), had its lowest engagement (89, 6.0% of reach). That is a single post, so read it as a caution, not a rule.

actions.title: Write the next 6 Reels as owner-level reframes, not industry case studies
actions.detail: Over the next two weeks, open each Reel with one claim any owner recognizes, shown as on-screen text in the first 2 seconds and repeated in the caption's first line. Then state the cost, then the fix, the way 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' and 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan…' do. Use industries only as examples inside the Reel, never as the hook. Keep posting in both Spanish and English. Before copying the top four, check whether any of them was boosted. The brief doesn't say, and their impressions-to-reach ratios (1.8–3.0) are higher than a typical Reel's (about 1.2–1.5).
actions.evidence: Owner-level Reels have a median of 11 engagements (27 posts) against 6 for single-industry Reels (12 posts), and all four posts above 500 reach used an owner-level hook. The Sep 9 dental and Sep 10 pharmacy posts reached 13 and 19 accounts.

actions.title: Co-publish Arqentia Reels as Collab posts with @rgschwart
actions.detail: Add @rgschwart as collaborator on 1 Arqentia Reel a week, with Rafael on camera speaking in the first person. Start by re-cutting the topic of 'Your business doesn't have a software problem' or 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan $287.000'. Stop after 2 if engagement on them falls well below @rgschwart's median of 125; its one work-only post got 89.
actions.evidence: @rgschwart's median reach is 1,347 per post (5 posts), against 110 for @arqentia.inc (55 posts), and it has 3,232 followers against 121. Collab posts have never been tried on either account, so the reach gain is unproven.

actions.title: Post on @rgschwart every two weeks and let the work show
actions.detail: Post next by Oct 4. Follow the shape of the Aug 26 post: photos from the last two weeks plus 2–3 lines on what you're building and what's hard. Don't pitch. One mention of the work is enough; leave the business explainers to Arqentia.
actions.evidence: 0 posts in the last 30 days and 2 in the last 90. Engagement went 89, 114, 125, 129, 176. 'This has been one of the busiest summers…' got 176 engagements and 7 shares, while the work-only Windy City post got 89. With only 5 posts, treat this as a direction, not a finding.

actions.title: Stop single-image posts and cap carousels at one a week
actions.detail: Move image slots to Reels. Keep one carousel a week, built like 'La meta no es trabajar más horas' (broad claim, then the cost, then 'tú solo apruebas') and posted Saturday afternoon, as a test of whether Sep 19 repeats. Don't post more single-industry carousels (dental, pharmacy, the AC checklist) until then.
actions.evidence: Images: 9 posts, median reach 34. Carousels: 7 posts, median reach 23, including the broad 'Most teams do not have a reporting problem…' (23) and '7 of 10 after-hours calls…' (34). Only Sep 19 broke out, at 548.

actions.title: Ask for shares, not comments, on the reach posts
actions.detail: End owner-level Reels by asking viewers to send the post on, for example 'Mándaselo a tu socio' or 'Send this to whoever runs your ops'. Keep the comment-KEYWORD call to action for one lead-magnet post a week. Judge that post on shares, saves, reach and the DMs it produces (tracked outside this brief), not on comment count.
actions.evidence: 0 comments across 7 posts in the last 30 days. 'Coméntalo' on the Sep 19 post got 0 comments on 548 reach. The one post that stated a principle, 'Most of the time, the problem is within the process design…', drew 20 of the account's 49 all-time shares.

recommendations.cadence: @arqentia.inc: 4 posts a week (3 Reels, 1 carousel), up from 5 posts in all of September and none since Sep 19. Slots: Sat 3–6pm (lift 1.5 on 3 posts: 'Es lunes a las 9…' 31, 'La meta no es…' 27, 'You didn't start this business' 10, all at or above the median of 9), Tue 6–9pm (lift 1.2, 4 posts), Wed 6–9pm (1.1, 2 posts) and Thu 12–3pm (1.0, 3 posts). Sat 6–9am also shows 1.5, but that rests on the Jul 25 post alone; the other two there got 9 and 4. Skip Friday (0.8 over 10 posts). The hour matters less than the hook here: 7–8am Reels had a median reach of 113, against 120 at other hours. @rgschwart: 1 post every two weeks. Its two Saturday posts landed at its median (125, 129) and its best post went out Wed 10am (176), so either slot works. The best-time table pools both accounts with only 2–4 posts per slot, so re-check it after 4 weeks.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, owner-level reframe hooks are what reach beyond the followers
working.evidence: All four posts above 500 reach open on a claim any owner recognizes: 'Your business doesn't have a software problem…' (Jul 25: 767 reach, 58 engagements, 6.4x the median of 9), 'OpenAI y Anthropic pagan $287.000…' (Aug 6: 724, 49), 'La meta no es trabajar más horas…' (Sep 19: 548, 27) and 'Es lunes a las 9 y estás comprando leads…' (Aug 8: 537, 31). Together they produced 2,576 of the account's 7,683 all-time reach. Three of the four are in Spanish, though only 13 of the 55 posts are.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, Reels are the only format that regularly gets past the 121 followers
working.evidence: 39 Reels: median reach 118, median 9 engagements. 7 carousels: median reach 23, median 5 engagements. 9 images: median reach 34, median 7 engagements.

working.point: On @arqentia.inc, a post that states a principle earned shares (sends), the signal Instagram weights most for reaching non-followers
working.evidence: 'Most of the time, the problem is within the process design…' (Jun 16) got 20 shares on 118 reach, or 17% sends per reach. That is 20 of the account's 49 all-time shares. Without it, the account's share rate is 0.38% of reach.

Engagements went 89, 114, 125, 129, 176 across its 5 posts (Nov 2025 to Aug 2026). 'This has been one of the busiest summers…' (Aug 26) got 176 engagements, which is 1.4x its median of 125 and 13.1% of reach. It also got 7 of the account's 16 all-time shares. Median reach is 1,347, or 42% of 3,232 followers.

recommendations.headline: On @arqentia.inc, go back to owner-level reframe Reels and stop leading with a single industry: all four posts that passed 500 reach opened on a claim any owner recognizes, while September's dental and pharmacy carousels reached 13 and 19 accounts.
recommendations.diagnosis: @arqentia.inc depends on a few owner-level posts. Four of its 55 posts produced 34% of its 7,683 all-time reach, and the rest sit near the median reach of 110, which is close to its 121 followers. In September that went the wrong way: the account posted 5 times (it had posted 15–17 times in each of June, July and August), leaned on single-industry Peru content and carousels, and saw median reach fall from 120 to 73 and comments fall to 0. @rgschwart is the opposite: it has 27x the followers, a median reach of 1,347 per post and engagement that rises with every post (89 to 176), but it hasn't posted since Aug 26 and has never posted a Reel. Rates here are on reach (Arqentia 8.2%, @rgschwart 9.8% all-time) rather than the brief's impressions basis (6.5%, 3.3%), because @rgschwart's carousels log about 3.3 impressions per account reached. The brief has no watch time, no follower-vs-non-follower split and no follower growth, and @rgschwart has only 5 posts, so data quality is limited.

experiments.test: Over the next 2 weeks, publish 2 Collab Reels with owner-level hooks and Rafael on camera, Saturday 3–6pm. Publish 2 solo Arqentia Reels in the same weeks to compare against.
experiments.metric: Reach against 110 (Arqentia median) and 1,347 (@rgschwart median); shares per reach; new @arqentia.inc followers in the 48 hours after each post.
experiments.hypothesis: Arqentia Reels posted as Collab posts with @rgschwart will reach well above Arqentia's median of 110 without falling far below @rgschwart's usual engagement.

experiments.test: Publish 2 Spanish carousels with the same structure (broad claim, cost, 'tú solo apruebas') on Saturday 3–6pm on consecutive weeks.
experiments.metric: Reach against the carousel median of 23; impressions-to-reach ratio (Sep 19 was 2.97, a sign Instagram showed it again); saves plus shares per reach.
experiments.hypothesis: The Sep 19 carousel's 548 reach came from its broad claim and its Saturday-afternoon slot, not from chance.

experiments.test: Publish 1 personal Reel (15–30 seconds, a real workday, hook as on-screen text in the first 2 seconds) within the next 2 weeks, in place of one carousel.
experiments.metric: Reach against the median of 1,347; engagements against the median of 125; follows gained.
experiments.hypothesis: A Reel on @rgschwart will reach past the 1,300–1,500 accounts its carousels reach, because Reels are shown to non-followers.
